book.ex: Exercise 1: Listen to the phone call.
book.q: Check the things that Carlos has done: learned to surf, fallen in the water a lot, surfed well, worn a life jacket, had an accident, been hang-gliding.
book.classNote: Do this in class with the audio (TR: 8.10).

book.q: How long has Carlos been at the camp? (and 4 more questions)

book.ex: Exercise 3: Discuss a vacation or camp that you enjoyed.
book.q: Work with a partner. Ask and answer questions. Use the words in the box.
book.answer: I went to the beach last year. It was totally awesome. · Really? What was the weather like?

book.q: Talk about your dream vacation. Use: if / would, would rather.
book.answer: If I went on vacation, I would go on a photo safari! · No way! I would rather go to a theme park!

book.q: Where / the Sphinx / build?
book.inst: Work with a partner. Take notes.
book.answer: Where was the Sphinx built? It was built in Egypt.
book.why: The question is the example in the book. The Sphinx is in Egypt.

book.q: How many / terra-cotta statues / make?
book.answer: How many terra-cotta statues were made? Thousands. More than 6,000 were discovered.

book.q: Who / the objects with the English gold / discover / by?
book.answer: Who were the objects with the English gold discovered by? They were discovered by archaeologists.

book.q: Win a point for each correct answer!
book.classNote: Do this in class with the audio (TR: 8.12).

sections.title: Let's Talk: I love it!

learn.title: I will…
lines: ↩️ bring the topic back on track

learn.title: Useful phrases
table: I love it! / I hate it.

learn.title: The conversation (short summary)
lines: Read the full conversation in your book. 📖
Three boys are ready to play a history game. One boy changes the topic: By the way, have you seen the new shark movie?
They talk about the movie: What's it like? It's awesome. I love it.
Then one boy brings them back: Anyway, let's talk about it later. Back to the game.

book.q: Listen to the conversation and read it in your book.
book.classNote: Do this in class with the audio (TR: 8.13).

book.q: Work in groups of three. Have a conversation. Use the chart. Take turns. Change the subject to something else.
book.answer: Is everyone ready to do our science project? · Yes! · Hey, before I forget, have you tried the new ice cream shop? · No. What's it like? · I love it! · Anyway, back to the project.

models: Is everyone ready to play the game?
By the way, have you seen the new shark movie?
No, I haven't. What's it like?
Anyway, let's talk about it later. Back to the game.

turns.q: Start a conversation with your group.
turns.example: Is everyone ready to start our English project?
By the way, have you played the new soccer game?

build: Is | everyone ready | to play | the game?
By the way, | have you seen | the new | shark movie?
Anyway, | let's talk | about it | later.

quiz.q: Which phrase brings the topic back?

sections.title: Let's Talk: Excuse me.

learn.title: Useful phrases
table: I think she said ___, but I'm not sure.
Sure. I'll go over it again.
Could I ask a question, please?
Could you say / explain that again?
No problem! I'll explain it again.

learn.title: The conversation (short summary)
lines: Read the full conversation in your book. 📖
Two students missed what the teacher said. One thinks they have to match pictures and sentences, but I'm not sure.
So they ask politely: Excuse me, Ms. Trujillo. Could you repeat that? The teacher says: Sure. I'll go over it again.

book.q: Listen to the conversation and read it in your book.
book.classNote: Do this in class with the audio (TR: 8.14).

book.q: You will hear two discussions. Circle the answers.
book.classNote: Do this in class with the audio (TR: 8.15).

book.q: Situation 1: Your teacher is going over the answers. You missed the last answer.
book.inst: Work in groups of three. Choose a situation and discuss.
book.answer: Hey, what did she say? I missed that. · I think she said "b," but I'm not sure. · Excuse me, T. Roy. Could you repeat the last answer? · Sure. I'll go over it again.

book.q: Situation 2: Your teacher is explaining tonight's homework. You didn't quite understand.
book.answer: Excuse me, could I ask a question, please? Could you explain the homework again? · No problem! I'll explain it again.

models: I think she said we have to match the pictures and sentences, but I'm not sure.
I missed it, too. Let's ask her.
Excuse me. Could you repeat that?
Sure. I'll go over it again.

turns.q: You didn't hear the teacher. Ask politely.
turns.example: Excuse me, T. Roy. Could you say that again, please?

turns.q: Your friend asks: What did he say? You aren't sure.
turns.starter: I think he said…, but I'm not sure.
turns.example: I think he said page 50, but I'm not sure.
